children: Shares of cybersecurity AI platform provider SentinelOne

jumped 6.9% in the morning session after the company announced a partnership with the Defence Cyber Command (DCCOM) of Singapore's Digital and Intelligence (DIS) to strengthen cyber defense and advance secure AI across Singapore's defense and critical infrastructure sectors.

According to the company's press release, the relationship was formalized at CIDEX 2026 on November 19, 2026. SentinelOne and DCCOM will explore combining the Singularity Platform, SentinelLABS AI and threat intelligence research and training with DCCOM's expertise to detect, investigate and respond to threats. The release noted that the Singularity Platform supports on-premise and air-gapped deployment for defense networks where a cloud connection is not an option.
Under the collaboration, the parties will explore partnering in cybersecurity technology and solutions, cyber threat intelligence sharing, research and innovation and training and capacity building.
What is the market telling us

SentinelOne’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 39 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was about 24 hours ago when the stock gained 8% on the news that Nvidia's quarterly beat and outlook spurred dip-buying in beaten-down cloud software, while fresh cybersecurity warnings lifted security vendors ahead of Palo Alto Networks' earnings. Nvidia beat third-quarter estimates and forecast 75% fiscal 2028 revenue growth, CNBC reported, helping the Nasdaq open 0.65% higher as AI-spending concerns eased, Reuters noted.

Even though Nvidia reversed below flat by mid-morning, the steadier tech open offered relief after the previous session's selloff.Security shares drew added support after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned in congressional testimony reported by Bloomberg that Iranian-backed actors have targeted U.S. financial, energy, and transportation systems, while CNBC noted recent Microsoft and FAA outages kept security spending in focus before Palo Alto Networks reports after the close.

SentinelOne is up 69% since the beginning of the year, and at $24.74 per share, it is trading close to its 52-week high of $26.27 from October 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of SentinelOne’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $351.93.
